perturbation_actually_applied.caveat: every shift is a multiple of 64, so op_return keeps line offset 0 and all handlers move together - relative distances are unchanged

verdict.rule: fib_rec variation < 1% -> reject 'the call path is highly layout sensitive' -> skip the Frame/Stack redesign -> go to native-recursive prototype
verdict.not_doing_B: 256 -> 128 with 107 consumer changes; the probe does not show Entry shrinking is worthless, it shows there is no evidence footprint is the bottleneck, so the change budget should not be spent first
verdict.not_doing_A: the 16-byte Stack cleanup crosses no cache line and removes no significant load; it is a refactor, not a Phase 4 item

observations.P4-01a: recursive_countdown_1 +0.78% at 4/4, attributed to placement after op_return shrank 1760 bytes

retrospective_caution.what_it_does_not_settle: both belong to the relative-displacement class this probe does not cover, so their attribution is not refuted; the most likely alternative is a real per-push or per-return mechanism cost, which remains unproven

route.rationale: four falsifications now converge: special state is not the four cache lines (P4-00), the 208-byte frame is not the extended chain (P4-01a), slice lengths are not pure redundancy (P4-02.0), and the call path is not address-layout sensitive (P4-01c) - while P3-13's split still puts 68% of the remaining gap in return, where qjs does a C return off an alloca frame

limits: one build instance per pad, so the compiler two-state effect (~0.4% measured earlier) is not separated and bounds this result's strength
